questions.q: What two root causes were behind the slow Oracle trial balance report, per this lesson?
options: A missing index on journal_date and stale optimizer statistics on GL_JOURNAL_LINES
The listener was down
The database was not in ARCHIVELOG mode
The fin_app_role was missing SELECT privileges
questions.explain: AWR pointed to a full table scan, traced to both a missing index and statistics that hadn't been refreshed as the table grew.

questions.q: What did EXPLAIN show for the slow MySQL orders lookup before the fix was applied?
options: type: ALL, indicating a full table scan because customer_email had no index
type: ref, indicating an index was already being used efficiently
A syntax error in the query
That the orders table did not exist
questions.explain: EXPLAIN showing type ALL means MySQL scanned the whole table; adding an index on customer_email changed the scan type to ref.

questions.q: What PostgreSQL view revealed that sales_fact had a bloat problem?
options: pg_stat_user_tables, showing n_dead_tup far higher than n_live_tup
pg_hba.conf
information_schema.tables
pg_stat_statements only
questions.explain: pg_stat_user_tables exposes live and dead tuple counts per table, which is how the bloat from heavy nightly upserts was identified.

questions.q: Why was autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor tuned specifically for the sales_fact table rather than changed globally?
options: sales_fact has an unusually heavy nightly upsert pattern that outruns the default 20% dead-row threshold, while other tables don't need that aggressive a setting
PostgreSQL does not allow per-table autovacuum settings
Global settings only apply to the reporting schema, not individual tables
It was a random choice with no technical justification
questions.explain: Per-table autovacuum tuning targets the specific table with the update-heavy workload without changing behavior for every other table in the database.

questions.q: Across all three incidents in this lesson, what discipline is applied identically even though the tools differ?
options: Measure, identify, change, verify
Always add an index first, regardless of the diagnosis
Restart the database server before investigating
Restore from the most recent backup
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly applies the same measure-identify-change-verify sequence to Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, using each platform's own diagnostic and fix tools.
